{"text": "Lilly’s margins do look like they were still expanding recently, but the desk cannot say they will keep expanding next year because it does not forecast.

What the filings do show is that the profit mix improved into 2025: “Net income and earnings per share increased in 2025, primarily due to higher gross margin, partially offset by increased marketing, selling, and administrative expenses and research and development expenses.” The same Item 7 also says revenue in 2025 was “driven primarily by increased volume, partially offset by lower realized prices,” which matters because it shows the operating setup is not all one-way margin expansion.

On the reported history, net margin moved from 19.7% [f_176e422745b8] in 2021 to 21.9% [f_176e422745b8] in 2022, then down to 15.4% [f_176e422745b8] in 2023, then up to 23.5% [f_176e422745b8] in 2024 and 31.7% [f_176e422745b8] in 2025. Over the last eight quarters it went from 26.2% [f_586328267192] to 37.4% [f_586328267192], though there was volatility in between, including 8.48% [f_586328267192] in 2024-09-30.

The revenue and cost lines support why margins improved: total revenues rose to $19.80B [f_b4b3d27da8f8] from $11.30B [f_b4b3d27da8f8] over the eight-quarter window, while cost of revenue rose more slowly, to $3.58B [f_392226a6c43f] from $2.17B [f_392226a6c43f]. Operating cash flow was also strong, reaching $5.33B [f_a0a64e39d278] in the latest quarter, though it was uneven across the period.

What this means for the book: the recent margin trend is clearly favorable, but it is not a clean, guaranteed continuation story. The filing itself flags two offsets to keep in mind: lower realized prices and rising marketing/selling/admin and R&D expense. So I would read LLY as a name where margin expansion is still supported by volume and gross margin improvement, but next year’s path depends on whether pricing pressure and expense growth stay contained.

One important limitation: the desk could not compute gross margin or operating margin for LLY from the available filed lines, because “LLY reports no gross_profit with a period” and “LLY reports no operating_income with a period.” So the evidence on margin expansion comes from net margin and the underlying revenue, cost, and filing discussion rather than those two margin series."}
